title: Warmer starts near 15 C were linked to shorter US bird survey times in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether survey-start temperature was linked to elapsed survey time in 64,710 accepted bird survey runs from Canada and the US in 1985-2024. Four country-period models controlled for route-observer effects, state-year effects, start time, date, wind, sky, and assistant status. At a 15 C start, a 5 C warmer temperature was linked to 0.97 minutes less survey time in US records from 2005-2024. The four-test interval was -1.57 to -0.37 minutes. Fair-weather, duration-limit, and route-trend checks kept this estimate negative. The other three main intervals included zero. Adding duration terms changed local temperature-richness slopes by 0.01-0.04 recorded taxa per 5 C. Elapsed time includes travel and recording. Selection, local conditions, shared routes, and changing detection limit inference. We do not estimate causal heat effects, climate change damage, or pollution. The package includes code, the derived panel, exact raw provenance, all results, checks, and a figure.

display.caption: Duration slopes at 15 C with four-test intervals, and secondary richness slopes with individual 95% intervals. Duration is elapsed time, including travel and recording.

citations.reason: We retrieve the source dictionary and review the start-temperature study. Raw observations overlap, but our outcome and models differ.
Its weather-richness models control for duration. We test elapsed time as an outcome with the same raw release.
